definition: Voluminous means very large in volume or quantity.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word voluminous. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know voluminous should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The circus tent is voluminous — three rings, a band pit, and seating for a thousand under one sweep of striped cloth.
A snug jacket touches at every seam; voluminous is its opposite pole, cloth to spare in every direction.
Roomy leaves comfortable space inside; voluminous goes further — folds on folds, fabric or files by the armful, volume past all mere comfort.

Bulky means big and awkward in the carrying — one clumsy object that fights the arms and jams the doorway, with no grace about it. Voluminous is abundance of volume, in folds or in files: cloth by the armful, letters by the shelf. A bulky crate; a voluminous cloak.

Billowing means swelling outward in soft folds as air moves through — sails filling, smoke rolling, curtains lifting at an open window. It is volume in motion. Voluminous is the volume itself, with everything still: a cloak folded flat in a trunk is not billowing, but it is every bit as voluminous.

Voluminous means very large in volume or quantity.

Aunt Marisol's handbag is voluminous in a way physics ought to question: it has yielded, on request, an umbrella, a sewing kit, two paperbacks, a thermos, and once — at a picnic short of dessert — an entire pineapple.
The bag swallows a full arm to the elbow and gives no sign of filling.
Voluminous is the bulk word: great volume, whether swallowed (a bag, a tent) or supplied (files, letters).
The root is Latin volumen, a scroll — writing rolled round and round until it filled the hand.
Anything voluminous fills like that: in rolls, folds, and armfuls.
Voluminous measures bulk: garments that billow, files that fill shelves, tents that swallow crowds.
Don't let the stereo mislead you — loud is about sound level, and a voluminous voice would be a big one only in a poet's joke.
Among its unit-mates, copious counts the pouring quantity, replete describes the well-stocked container, and voluminous weighs the sheer roll and fold of the thing itself.
